Thus no vertices with neighborhood $\{a,b,d\}$ or $\{a,c,d\}$ remain.

Suppose $n_e=3$. The table gives one nonplanar completion
$B+E'$. It is a $K_5$-minor-free minor of $G$: contract $\Psi_3$
to triangles and $bd$ into $d$, then retain only $B+E'$.
Take a $K_{3,3}$ subdivision in it and apply
Lemma~\ref{core:retained-subdivision} with attachments $a,c,d,e$
and added edges $E'$.
The reduction keeps the interior connected, all four attachments
and the failed test. The same table therefore keeps the whole
graph nontoroidal, so minimality leaves $B$ unchanged.
Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} gives $9{,}127$
possibilities for $B$ without $cd$ and $8{,}967$ with $cd$.
Every resulting graph has a proper nontoroidal minor obtained
by deleting or contracting one edge~\supp{E29}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ...
